ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE MANAGEMENT OF INTERNATIONAL AVIATION CARBON EMISSIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Management of International Aviation Carbon Emissions and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Formulation and Implementation of Master Plans)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall formulate a plan for the management of international aviation carbon emissions under Article 5 (1) of the Act on the Management of International Aviation Carbon Emissions (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as a "master plan") by December 31 of the year preceding the year in which the master plan is to be implemented.
(2) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport intends to formulate or amend a master plan, the Minister shall undergo deliberation by the Aviation Policy Committee under Article 4 of the Aviation Business Act; provided, this shall not apply where any of the following matters is amended:
1. Matters under Article 5 (2) 1 and 3 of the Act;
2. Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, including education and publicity concerning the management of international aviation carbon emissions, among the matters under Article 5 (2) 4 of the Act.
(3) Where necessary to formulate a master plan, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may hear opinions from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of organizations and institutions related to international aviation or request them to submit materials concerning the management of international aviation carbon emissions.
(4) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport has formulated or amended a master plan, the Minister shall publicly announce its details in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 3 (Formulation and Implementation of Implementation Plans)
(1) The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall formulate a detailed implementation plan under Article 5 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") by December 31 of the year preceding the year in which the implementation plan is to be implemented.
(2) An implementation plan shall include the following:
1. Matters concerning international aviation carbon emissions of obligated operators (meaning aircraft operators that are required to offset and reduce international aviation carbon emissions after being designated and publicly notified under Article 6 (1) of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply);
2. Matters concerning obligated operators' performance in offsetting and reducing international aviation carbon emissions and their plans to offset and reduce international aviation carbon emissions in the following year;
3. Other matters that the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems necessary to include in an implementation plan to facilitate implementation of the master plan.
(3) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport formulates an implementation plan under paragraph (1), the Minister shall evaluate the performance of the preceding year's implementation plan and reflect the results therein.
(4) Where necessary to facilitate implementation of the master plan, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may amend an implementation plan formulated under paragraph (1).
(5) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport has formulated or amended an implementation plan, the Minister shall publicly announce its details in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 4 (Designation of Verification Bodies)
(1) "Standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, including personnel and facilities" in Article 7 (1) of the Act means the following standards: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Having at least three persons who are verification auditors under Article 24-3 (1) of the Act on the Allocation and Trading of Greenhouse-Gas Emission Permits and who meet all of the following requirements (hereinafter referred to as "verification auditors"):
(a) Their specialized field shall be the aviation field under Article 41 (1) and item 1 (g) of attached Table 5 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Allocation and Trading of Greenhouse-Gas Emission Permits or the common field under item 1 (h) of that Table;
(b) They shall have completed education on the management of international aviation carbon emissions prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment;
2. Securing an office necessary to perform verification work through ownership, lease, or other means;
3. Being a corporation that has liability insurance with coverage of at least one billion won in connection with verification of greenhouse-gas emissions.
(2) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment has designated an international aviation carbon emissions verification body under Article 7 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "verification body"), the Minister shall post the details on the website and issue a certificate of designation as a verification body to the relevant body. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), details concerning procedures for designating verification bodies, etc. shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 5 (Operational Standards for Verification Bodies)
"Operational standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the prohibition against entrusting verification work to another body" in Article 7 (2) of the Act means the operational standards for verification bodies in attached Table 1.

Article 6 (Revocation of Designation of Verification Bodies)
(1) The standards for administrative dispositions, including revocation of designation of verification bodies under Article 7 (3) of the Act, shall be as specified in attached Table 2.
(2) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment revokes the designation of a verification body under Article 7 (3) of the Act, the Minister shall notify the relevant verification body thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Where its designation is revoked under paragraph (2), a verification body shall return its certificate of designation as a verification body to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 7 (Submission and Evaluation of Results of Verification Work)
(1) Pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act, a verification body shall prepare the results of its verification work for each half-year and submit them to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may conduct regular evaluations of the appropriateness of the results submitted under paragraph (1); provided, where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment deems it necessary, the Minister may obtain additional materials and conduct evaluations as occasion requires. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment has conducted an evaluation under paragraph (2), the Minister may disclose all or part of the evaluation results within three months from the date the evaluation is completed. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), details concerning submission and evaluation of the results of verification work, etc. shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 8 (Preparation and Verification of Emissions Reports)
(1) An obligated operator shall calculate the international aviation carbon emissions emitted through international operations during the preceding year according to the methods for calculating international aviation carbon emissions in attached Table 3 and reflect them in the emissions report under Article 8 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "emissions report").
(2) Where, as a result of verifying an emissions report commissioned by an obligated operator under Article 8 (2) of the Act, any of the following applies, a verification body may request the obligated operator to supplement the emissions report:
1. Where any matter specified in the subparagraphs of Article 8 (2) of the Act is omitted from the emissions report;
2. Where measurements of aviation fuel consumption, international aviation carbon emissions, etc. were not made according to the monitoring plan approved under Article 6 (2) of the Act;
3. Where the international aviation carbon emissions calculated by the obligated operator according to attached Table 3 do not match those calculated by the verification body according to that Table.
(3) A verification report on the conformity of an emissions report under Article 8 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "emissions verification report") shall include all of the following:
1. The name of the verification body and the names of the verification auditors who participated in the verification;
2. The verification criteria for the emissions report;
3. Matters discovered during the verification process and details of the measures taken in response;
4. The final verification opinion on the emissions report;
5. Other matters that the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems necessary to include in the emissions verification report.
(4) Where an obligated operator or verification body is requested by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to correct an emissions report or emissions verification report under the latter part of Article 8 (4) of the Act, it shall reflect the corrections in the emissions report or emissions verification report and submit it to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within 30 days from the date it receives the request for correction.
(5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), details necessary for preparation of emissions reports and emissions verification reports, etc. shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 9 (Exemption from Fulfillment of Offsetting Obligations)
(1) "Cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as where the quantity required to be offset is below a certain threshold" in the proviso of Article 10 (1) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Where the total quantity that the obligated operator was notified to offset under Article 9 (1) of the Act for the immediately preceding compliance period (meaning each three-year period counted from 2021; hereinafter the same shall apply) is less than 3,000 tons;
2. Where December 31 of the third year, including the first year in which a license for international air transport business was obtained under Article 7 (1) of the Aviation Business Act, has not passed, and the total international aviation carbon emissions emitted since commencement of international operations do not exceed one one-thousandth of the 2019 global international aviation carbon emissions specified in the Convention on International Civil Aviation and Annex 16 thereto.
(2) Details, including the scope of exemption from fulfillment of offsetting obligations in the cases specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 10 (Preparation and Verification of Reports on Fulfillment of Offsetting Obligations)
(1) An obligated operator shall reflect the details of its fulfillment of offsetting obligations under the main clause of Article 10 (1) of the Act in the report on fulfillment of offsetting obligations under paragraph (2) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as an "offsetting obligation fulfillment report").
(2) Where, as a result of verifying an offsetting obligation fulfillment report commissioned by an obligated operator under Article 10 (2) of the Act, any matter specified in the subparagraphs of that paragraph is omitted from the report, a verification body may request the obligated operator to supplement the offsetting obligation fulfillment report.
(3) A verification report on the conformity of an offsetting obligation fulfillment report under Article 10 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "offsetting obligation fulfillment verification report") shall include all of the following:
1. The name of the verification body and the names of the verification auditors who participated in the verification;
2. The verification criteria for the offsetting obligation fulfillment report;
3. Matters discovered during the verification process and details of the measures taken in response;
4. The final verification opinion on the offsetting obligation fulfillment report;
5. Other matters that the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport deems necessary to include in the offsetting obligation fulfillment verification report.
(4) Where an obligated operator or verification body is requested by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to correct an offsetting obligation fulfillment report or offsetting obligation fulfillment verification report under the latter part of Article 10 (4) of the Act, it shall reflect the corrections in the relevant report and submit it to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within 30 days from the date it receives the request for correction.
(5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), details necessary for preparation of offsetting obligation fulfillment reports and offsetting obligation fulfillment verification reports, etc. shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 11 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority or Duties)
(1) Pursuant to Article 15 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall delegate the following authority to the President of the National Institute of Environmental Research: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Designation and revocation of designation of verification bodies, suspension of their operations, and corrective orders under Article 7 (1) and (3) of the Act;
2. Receipt and evaluation of results of verification work and disclosure of evaluation results under Article 7 (4) of the Act;
3. Fact-finding surveys on the matters specified in subparagraphs 2 and 3 of Article 14 of the Act (limited to matters concerning verification by verification bodies).
(2) Pursuant to Article 15 (2) of the Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall entrust the following duties to the Korea Transportation Safety Authority under the Korea Transportation Safety Authority Act:
1. Investigation and analysis of materials concerning the adoption and amendment of the Convention on International Civil Aviation and Annex 16 thereto under Article 3 (2) of the Act;
2. Investigation and analysis of international conventions and materials from foreign governments, etc. related to the management of international aviation carbon emissions under Article 3 (2) of the Act;
3. Preliminary review for approval of monitoring plans and approval of amendments thereto under Article 6 (2) of the Act;
4. Review of the appropriateness of emissions reports and emissions verification reports under the latter part of Article 8 (4) of the Act;
5. Calculation of quantities required to be offset under Article 9 (1) of the Act;
6. Calculation of international aviation carbon emissions and quantities required to be offset under the former part of Article 9 (2) of the Act;
7. Review of the appropriateness of offsetting obligation fulfillment reports and offsetting obligation fulfillment verification reports under the latter part of Article 10 (4) of the Act.

Article 12 (Administrative Fines)
The standards for imposing administrative fines under Article 18 (1) and (2) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 4.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 34849, Aug. 20, 2024>

This Decree shall enter into force on August 21, 2024.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 35811, Oct. 1, 2025>
(Presidential Decree Partially Amending 306 Statutes and Regulations to Reflect Government Reorganization)

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, among the Presidential Decrees amended by this Decree, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that were promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall enter into force on the enforcement dates of the respective Presidential Decrees.
